context_of_use: Comparative synthetic engineering evidence for ECG R-peak detection and beat-to-beat RR robustness across a paired, escalating composite noise frontier.

limitations: Synthetic signals do not establish clinical sensitivity, specificity, population generalization, or diagnostic safety.
A PASS applies only to the exact package, evidence level, verifier, algorithm build, submission, and hashes recorded in the evidence bundle.
The cited sources inform design and interpretation; none directly specifies the complete Synsigra case matrix and numeric gate set.
evidence_basis.numeric_threshold_basis: Pack-author pre-specified engineering gates selected for discrimination, regression stability, and the exact deterministic protocol; no numeric gate is copied from a cited standard or study.
evidence_basis.rationale: Long deterministic cases probe R-peak performance across severe, calibrated noise. The exact signals, +/-50 ms matching, SNR ladder, and F1 gates form a Synsigra frontier test and are not direct reproductions of a cited benchmark.

sources.citation: Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation. Testing and reporting performance results of cardiac rhythm and ST segment measurement algorithms. 2012, reaffirmed 2020.
sources.limitation: The public scope page does not supply transferable Synsigra PASS/FAIL values, and Synsigra does not claim EC57 conformity.
sources.relevance: Establishes the relevant testing-and-reporting scope for cardiac rhythm and ST-segment algorithms.
sources.title: ANSI/AAMI EC57:2012/(R)2020

sources.citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Recognized Consensus Standard 3-155, IEC 60601-2-47 Edition 2.0, ambulatory electrocardiographic systems.
sources.limitation: Recognition of a device-system standard does not make a synthetic pack conformant and does not supply Synsigra's numerical gates.
sources.relevance: Confirms the recognized safety and essential-performance scope for ambulatory ECG systems with analysis algorithms.
sources.title: FDA recognition of IEC 60601-2-47:2012

sources.citation: Moody GB. bxb(1), WFDB Applications Guide. Updated 10 June 2022.
sources.limitation: Synsigra deliberately uses a tighter +/-50 ms event window and a different scorer, so results are not bxb or EC57 results.
sources.relevance: Defines sensitivity, positive predictive value, beat matching, and the default 150 ms bxb match window used in EC57 reporting.
sources.title: WFDB bxb beat-by-beat comparator

sources.citation: Moody GB, Muldrow WE, Mark RG. A noise stress test for arrhythmia detectors. Computers in Cardiology. 1984;11:381-384. PhysioNet version 1.0.0.
sources.limitation: Synsigra's deterministic continuous and composite noise cases, especially below -6 dB, are not NSTDB records and are not directly performance-comparable to that database.
sources.relevance: Provides ambulatory baseline-wander, muscle, and electrode-motion noise and calibrated noisy intervals down to -6 dB SNR.
sources.title: MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database v1.0.0

sources.citation: Reklewski W, Miskowicz M. Sensors. 2024;24(5):1698. doi:10.3390/s24051698.
sources.limitation: Its tested detectors, signals, noise injection, and tolerances differ from Synsigra and do not define Synsigra gate values.
sources.relevance: Shows that reported QRS performance changes with temporal tolerance, noise level, and morphology, supporting explicit multidimensional protocol disclosure.
sources.title: QRS Detector Performance Evaluation Aware of Temporal Accuracy and Presence of Noise

sources.citation: Kristof J et al. PLOS Digital Health. 2024;3:e0000538. doi:10.1371/journal.pdig.0000538.
sources.limitation: Observed F1 values are dataset- and protocol-specific and are not universal acceptance limits.
sources.relevance: Reports quality-stratified QRS benchmarking with a disclosed +/-75 ms matching rule and demonstrates large quality effects.
sources.title: QRS detection in single-lead, telehealth electrocardiogram signals: benchmarking open-source algorithms

evidence_boundary: Synthetic comparative R-peak and beat-to-beat RR engineering evidence only; the SNR ladder is not a patient-noise prevalence model, clinical validation, diagnostic performance evidence, or regulatory qualification.

evidence_profile.description: A permissive engineering gate for baseline implementations. It is not a clinical, regulatory, or algorithm-class claim.
evidence_profile.threshold_adjustment: Relative to Level 2: minimum gates are reduced by 0.10 (floor 0); maximum error gates are multiplied by 1.25.

truth_policy.aggregation: Each SNR case has its own acceptance stratum. Pooled results cannot compensate for a failed tier.
truth_policy.event_scoreability: All additive calibrated-noise, baseline-wander and powerline intervals remain scoreable. Only physically truncated record-boundary QRS truth is excluded.
truth_policy.first_beat: Excluded because no preceding in-record R peak exists for RR construction.
truth_policy.paired_design: The eight noisy scenarios use the same cardiac timebase, deterministic PVC cadence, interval schedule and noise source offsets; only target SNR and analytic artifact severities increase.
truth_policy.rr_definition: Difference between consecutive present-QRS construction R-peak times inside the record; an interval touching unscoreable R-peak truth is not_evaluable.
truth_policy.scope: R-peak event and RR measurement files are required. Signal-quality labels and HRV are explicitly outside the evidence matrix.
truth_policy.snr_definition: Target SNR is 20 log10(clean AC RMS / added-noise RMS), calibrated independently for every selected lead and interval. More-negative values are harder.
truth_policy.threshold_basis: Thresholds are a monotone, pre-specified engineering policy for this exact composite synthetic protocol. They are not universal clinical, classical-algorithm or deep-learning performance claims.
